note: Read 2026-10-30 on the Seychelles Licensing Authority's own page, Local Driving License. A resident applies to the SLA with a competency certificate from the Commissioner of Police (or a valid foreign driving permit) and pays a licence fee of SR 500 for 10 years. The class table gives Class 2, private vehicles including commercial vehicles not over 2,000 kg, from 18 years. The page names no learner's or provisional stage held by the SLA (the police's competency certificate comes before the licence), so 18 is held as the age of the licence itself. A non-resident applying for a local licence produces a foreign licence, what the page calls a 'Government Occupancy Permit (GOP)', a Seychelles ID card and a passport; the page names no different fee for them, so no foreign fee is held. A duplicate is SR 50 (not held). No identity card is issued by the SLA, and the page lists no exchange agreements (a foreign licence stands in for the competency certificate, from any country: not held as an exchange list).

sources.title: Seychelles Licensing Authority, Local Driving License
sources.said: When residents are applying for a local driving license, the applicant must: ... Attach a Competency Certificate from the Commissioner of Police that the applicant is capable of driving and fully controlling the vehicle in respect of which the application is made or a valid foreign driving permit. ... License fee of SR 500 for 10 years. ... Class 2 ... (18 year+) ... Private vehicles including commercial vehicle not exceeding 2000kg
